questions.topic: GST rate from CGST
questions.question: For an intra-state sale, the CGST paid by a dealer to the Central government is ₹120. If the marked price of the article is ₹2000, the rate of GST is:
questions.solution: For an intra-state sale, CGST = SGST, so Total GST = 2 × CGST = 2 × 120 = ₹240. Rate of GST = (240 × 100)/2000 = 12%.

questions.topic: Remainder theorem
questions.question: What must be subtracted from the polynomial x³ + x² − 2x + 1, so that the result is exactly divisible by (x − 3)?
questions.solution: Put x = 3 in P(x) = x³ + x² − 2x + 1: P(3) = 27 + 9 − 6 + 1 = 31. By the remainder theorem, 31 must be subtracted so that the result is exactly divisible by (x − 3).

questions.topic: Nature of roots (discriminant)
concepts: Discriminant zero for real and equal roots
questions.question: The roots of the quadratic equation px² − qx + r = 0 are real and equal if:
questions.solution: Comparing with ax² + bx + c = 0: a = p, b = −q, c = r. For real and equal roots, D = b² − 4ac = 0 ⇒ (−q)² − 4pr = 0 ⇒ q² = 4pr.

questions.topic: Median of ungrouped data
concepts: Median for even number of observations
questions.question: The median of the following observations arranged in ascending order is 64. Find the value of x: 27, 31, 46, 52, x, x + 4, 71, 79, 85, 90
questions.solution: N = 10 (even), so median = (5th term + 6th term)/2 = (x + x + 4)/2 = 64 ⇒ 2x + 4 = 128 ⇒ 2x = 124 ⇒ x = 62.

questions.topic: Direct proportion (uniform speed)
questions.question:
The given table shows the distance covered and the time taken by a train moving at a uniform speed along a straight track.
Distance (in m): 60 | 90 | y
Time (in s): 2 | x | 5
The values of x and y are:
questions.solution: At uniform speed distance ∝ time, so 60/2 = 90/x = y/5. From 60/2 = 90/x: x = 3. From 60/2 = y/5: y = 150.

questions.topic: nth term of an A.P.
questions.question: The 7th term of the given Arithmetic Progression (A.P.): 1/a, (1/a + 1), (1/a + 2), ... is:
questions.solution: First term A = 1/a; common difference d = (1/a + 1) − 1/a = 1. So A₇ = A + (7 − 1)d = 1/a + 6(1) = 1/a + 6.

questions.topic: Shares at a discount — sum invested
concepts: Sum invested = price × number of shares
questions.question: The sum invested to purchase 15 shares of a company of nominal value ₹75 available at a discount of 20% is:
questions.solution: Discounted price per share = 75 × (1 − 0.20) = 75 × 0.80 = ₹60. Sum invested = 60 × 15 = ₹900.

questions.topic: Circumcentre of a triangle
concepts: Circumcentre is equidistant from the vertices
questions.question: The circumcentre of a triangle is the point which is:

options.a: at equal distance from the three sides of the triangle.
options.b: at equal distance from the three vertices of the triangle.
options.c: the point of intersection of the three medians.
options.d: the point of intersection of the three altitudes of the triangle.

questions.solution: The circumcentre of a triangle is equidistant from all three vertices of the triangle (it is the centre of the circle passing through the vertices).

marking_points.point: Equidistant from the three vertices → option (b)

questions.topic: Validity of trigonometric identities
questions.question: Statement 1: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1. Statement 2: cosec²θ + cot²θ = 1. Which of the following is valid?
questions.solution: Statement 1 is a standard identity and is true. Statement 2 is invalid because the correct identity is cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1. Hence only Statement 1 is valid.

marking_points.point: Only Statement 1 is a valid identity → option (a)

questions.topic: Tangents from an external point, alternate angles

questions.question: In the given diagram, PS and PT are the tangents to the circle. SQ ∥ PT and ∠SPT = 80°. The value of ∠QST is:
questions.solution: PS = PT (tangents from an external point are equal) ⇒ ∠PST = ∠PTS (angles opposite equal sides). In ΔPST: ∠PST + ∠PTS + 80° = 180° ⇒ ∠PST = ∠PTS = 50°. Since SQ ∥ PT, ∠QST = ∠PTS = 50° (alternate angles).

questions.topic: Probability of an even number on a die
questions.question: Assertion (A): A die is thrown once and the probability of getting an even number is 2/3. Reason (R): The sample space for even numbers on a die is {2, 4, 6}.

options.a: A is true, R is false.
options.b: A is false, R is true.
options.c: Both A and R are true.
options.d: Both A and R are false.

questions.solution: When a die is thrown, P(even number) = 3/6 = 1/2, not 2/3, so the Assertion is false. The even numbers on a die are indeed {2, 4, 6}, so the Reason is true.

marking_points.point: P(even) = 1/2 so A false; R true → option (b)

questions.topic: Curved surface area of cylinders formed by rotating a sheet
concepts: Rotation of a rectangle forms a cylinder
questions.question: A rectangular sheet of paper of size 11 cm × 7 cm is first rotated about the side 11 cm and then about the side 7 cm to form a cylinder, as shown in the diagram. The ratio of their curved surface areas is:
questions.solution: Rotated about the 11 cm side: height h = 7 cm and circumference 2πR = 11 cm, so CSA = 2πR × h = 11 × 7 = 77 cm². Rotated about the 7 cm side: height H = 11 cm and circumference 2πr = 7 cm, so CSA = 7 × 11 = 77 cm². Ratio = 77 : 77 = 1 : 1.

questions.topic: Similarity with angle bisectors
questions.question: In the given diagram, ΔABC ~ ΔPQR. If AD and PS are bisectors of ∠BAC and ∠QPR respectively, then:
questions.solution: ΔABC ~ ΔPQR ⇒ ∠A = ∠P and ∠B = ∠Q. Since AD and PS bisect ∠BAC and ∠QPR, (1/2)∠A = (1/2)∠P ⇒ ∠BAD = ∠QPS. In ΔABD and ΔPQS: ∠B = ∠Q and ∠BAD = ∠QPS, so by AA similarity ΔABD ~ ΔPQS.

questions.topic: Surface area of a cylinder cut into halves; cost of painting
concepts: New rectangular faces created by the cut
questions.question: A solid metallic cylinder is cut into two identical halves along its height (as shown in the diagram). The diameter of the cylinder is 7 cm and the height is 10 cm. Find: (a) the total surface area (both the halves), (b) the total cost of painting the two halves at the rate of ₹30 per cm². (Use π = 22/7)
questions.solution: r = 7/2 cm, h = 10 cm, d = 7 cm. (a) Total surface area of both halves = total surface area of the whole cylinder + area of the two rectangular cut faces = 2πr(h + r) + 2dh = 2 × (22/7) × (7/2) × (10 + 7/2) + 2 × 7 × 10 = 22 × (27/2) + 140 = 297 + 140 = 437 cm². (b) Total cost of painting = total surface area × rate = 437 × 30 = ₹13,110 (the printed solution states ₹13,100, an arithmetic slip).

marking_points.point: Setup: TSA of both halves = 2πr(h + r) + 2dh (includes the two cut faces)

questions.topic: nth term and sum of a G.P.
concepts: Sum of n terms of G.P.
questions.question: 15, 30, 60, 120, ... are in G.P. (Geometric Progression). (a) Find the nth term of this G.P. in terms of n. (b) How many terms of the above G.P. will give the sum 945?
questions.solution: First term a = 15, common ratio r = 30/15 = 2. (a) aₙ = a·rⁿ⁻¹ = 15 × 2ⁿ⁻¹. (b) Sum of n terms: S = a(rⁿ − 1)/(r − 1) ⇒ 945 = 15(2ⁿ − 1)/(2 − 1) ⇒ 63 = 2ⁿ − 1 ⇒ 2ⁿ = 64 = 2⁶ ⇒ n = 6. So 6 terms of the G.P. give the sum 945.

marking_points.point: a = 15, r = 2 and nth term aₙ = 15 × 2ⁿ⁻¹

questions.topic: Factorization of sin³θ + cos³θ and identity proof
questions.question: Factorize: sin³θ + cos³θ. Hence, prove the following identity: (sin³θ + cos³θ)/(sinθ + cosθ) + sinθ·cosθ = 1
questions.solution: Using a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²): sin³θ + cos³θ = (sinθ + cosθ)(sin²θ − sinθ·cosθ + cos²θ) = (sinθ + cosθ)(1 − sinθ·cosθ), since sin²θ + cos²θ = 1. Then LHS = (sinθ + cosθ)(1 − sinθ·cosθ)/(sinθ + cosθ) + sinθ·cosθ = 1 − sinθ·cosθ + sinθ·cosθ = 1 = RHS. Hence proved.

marking_points.point: Factorize using a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²)
Simplify to (sinθ + cosθ)(1 − sinθ·cosθ) using sin²θ + cos²θ = 1

questions.topic: Tangents, alternate segment theorem, angle at centre, cyclic quadrilateral
concepts: Angle at centre = 2 × angle at circumference
questions.question: In the given diagram, O is the centre of the circle. PR and PT are two tangents drawn from the external point P and touching the circle at Q and S respectively. MN is a diameter of the circle. Given ∠PQM = 42° and ∠PSM = 25°. Find: (a) ∠OQM, (b) ∠QNS, (c) ∠QOS, (d) ∠QMS.
questions.solution: (a) OQ ⊥ PR (radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact), so ∠OQP = 90° ⇒ ∠OQM = 90° − 42° = 48°. (Similarly ∠OSM = 90° − 25° = 65°.) (b) By the alternate segment theorem, ∠QNM = ∠PQM = 42° and ∠SNM = ∠PSM = 25°, so ∠QNS = 42° + 25° = 67°. (c) ∠QOS = 2 × ∠QNS = 2 × 67° = 134° (angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference). (d) QMSN is a cyclic quadrilateral, so ∠QMS + ∠QNS = 180° ⇒ ∠QMS = 180° − 67° = 113°.
questions.figure_desc: Circle with centre O; tangent rays PR and PT from external point P touch the circle at Q (upper) and S (lower); MN is a diameter with M near P's side and N on the far side; chords QM, QN, QS, SM, SN drawn; 42° marked at Q between tangent and chord QM, 25° at S between tangent and chord SM.

questions.topic: Recurring deposit — finding the time
questions.question: Suresh has a recurring deposit account in a bank. He deposits ₹2000 per month and the bank pays interest at the rate of 8% per annum. If he gets ₹1040 as interest at the time of maturity, find in years total time for which the account was held.
questions.solution: P = ₹2000 per month, r = 8%, I = ₹1040. Let the duration be n months. I = P × n(n+1)/(2 × 12) × r/100 ⇒ 1040 = 2000 × n(n+1)/24 × 8/100 ⇒ n(n+1) = 156 = 12 × 13 ⇒ n = 12. So the account was held for 12 months, i.e. 1 year.

marking_points.point: Correct RD interest formula with P = 2000, r = 8, I = 1040

questions.topic: Mean by step-deviation method
questions.question:
The following table gives the duration of movies in minutes.
Duration (in minutes): 100-110 | 110-120 | 120-130 | 130-140 | 140-150 | 150-160
No. of movies: 5 | 10 | 17 | 8 | 6 | 4
Using step-deviation method, find the mean duration of the movies.
questions.solution: Mid-values xᵢ: 105, 115, 125, 135, 145, 155. Take assumed mean A = 125, class interval h = 10, uᵢ = (xᵢ − A)/h = −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3. fᵢuᵢ = −10, −10, 0, 8, 12, 12. Σfᵢ = 50, Σfᵢuᵢ = 12. Mean = A + (Σfᵢuᵢ/Σfᵢ) × h = 125 + (12/50) × 10 = 125 + 2.4 = 127.4 minutes.

marking_points.point: Correct table of xᵢ, uᵢ and fᵢuᵢ with A = 125, h = 10

questions.topic: Componendo and dividendo
questions.question: If (a + b)³/(a − b)³ = 64/27: (a) Find (a + b)/(a − b). (b) Hence using properties of proportion, find a : b.
questions.solution: (a) Taking cube root on both sides: (a + b)/(a − b) = 4/3. (b) Applying componendo and dividendo: [(a + b) + (a − b)]/[(a + b) − (a − b)] = (4 + 3)/(4 − 3) ⇒ 2a/2b = 7/1 ⇒ a/b = 7/1. So a : b = 7 : 1.

questions.topic: Two angles of elevation on opposite sides
concepts: Distances on opposite sides of a tower
questions.question: The angle of elevation of the top of a 100 m high tree from two points A and B on the opposite side of the tree are 52° and 45° respectively. Find the distance AB, to the nearest metre.
questions.solution:
AB ≈ 178 m
Let the tree be CD (height 100 m) with foot C between A and B.
In ΔADC: tan 52° = DC/AC ⇒ 1.2799 = 100/AC ⇒ AC = 100/1.2799 = 78.13 m.
In ΔBDC: tan 45° = DC/BC ⇒ 1 = 100/BC ⇒ BC = 100 m.
AB = AC + BC = 78.13 + 100 = 178.13 m ≈ 178 m (to the nearest metre).

questions.topic: AA similarity, Pythagoras, ratio of areas
questions.question: In the given diagram ΔADB and ΔACB are two right angled triangles with ∠ADB = ∠BCA = 90°. If AB = 10 cm, AD = 6 cm, BC = 2.4 cm and DP = 4.5 cm: (a) Prove that ΔAPD ~ ΔBPC. (b) Find the length of BD and PB. (c) Hence, find the length of PA. (d) Find area ΔAPD : area ΔBPC.
questions.solution: (a) In ΔAPD and ΔBPC: ∠ADP = ∠BCP = 90° and ∠APD = ∠BPC (vertically opposite angles). So by AA similarity, ΔAPD ~ ΔBPC. (b) From similarity, AD/BC = DP/CP ⇒ 6/2.4 = 4.5/CP ⇒ CP = 1.8 cm. In right ΔBPC: BP² = BC² + CP² = (2.4)² + (1.8)² = 5.76 + 3.24 = 9 ⇒ BP = 3 cm. BD = DP + PB = 4.5 + 3 = 7.5 cm. (c) In right ΔADP: PA² = AD² + DP² = 36 + 20.25 = 56.25 ⇒ PA = 7.5 cm. (d) Area ΔAPD : Area ΔBPC = (1/2 × 4.5 × 6)/(1/2 × 2.4 × 1.8) = 13.5/2.16 = 25/4. Required ratio is 25 : 4.

marking_points.point: AA similarity proof (right angles + vertically opposite angles)
CP = 1.8 cm, PB = 3 cm, BD = 7.5 cm

questions.topic: Angle at centre, isosceles triangle in a circle, alternate segment
concepts: Angle at centre = 2 × angle at circumference
questions.question: In the given diagram, an isosceles ΔABC is inscribed in a circle with centre O. PQ is a tangent to the circle at C. OM is perpendicular to chord AC and ∠COM = 65°. Find: (a) ∠ABC, (b) ∠BAC, (c) ∠BCQ.
questions.solution: Since OM ⊥ chord AC, OM bisects ∠AOC (ΔAOC is isosceles with OA = OC), so ∠AOC = ∠AOM + ∠COM = 65° + 65° = 130°. (a) ∠ABC = (1/2)∠AOC = (1/2) × 130° = 65° (angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference). (b) ΔABC is isosceles with AB = AC, so ∠ACB = ∠ABC = 65°. Then ∠BAC = 180° − 65° − 65° = 50°. (c) ∠BCQ = ∠BAC = 50° (angle between tangent and chord equals the angle in the alternate segment).
questions.figure_desc: Circle centre O with inscribed isosceles triangle ABC (tick marks show AB = AC, A at top, B lower-left, C lower-right); M on chord AC with OM ⊥ AC; 65° marked twice at O (∠AOM and ∠COM); line PQ tangent to the circle at C. The equal sides (AB = AC) are indicated only in the figure.

questions.topic: Compound inequation in integers; number line
questions.question: Solve the following inequation, write down the solution set and represent it on the real number line: −3 + x ≤ 7x/2 + 2 < 8 + 2x, x ∈ I
questions.solution: First part: −3 + x ≤ 7x/2 + 2 ⇒ −3 + x ≤ (7x + 4)/2 ⇒ −6 + 2x ≤ 7x + 4 ⇒ −10 ≤ 5x ⇒ x ≥ −2 ...(i). Second part: 7x/2 + 2 < 8 + 2x ⇒ (7x + 4)/2 < 8 + 2x ⇒ 7x + 4 < 16 + 4x ⇒ 3x < 12 ⇒ x < 4 ...(ii). From (i) and (ii): −2 ≤ x < 4, x ∈ I. Solution set = {−2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3}, shown on the number line with solid dots at −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3.

marking_points.point: Solution set {−2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3} with correct number line

questions.topic: Coordinates from a graph, centroid, section formula, equation of a line
questions.question: In the given diagram, ABC is a triangle, where B(4, −4) and C(−4, −2). D is a point on AC. (a) Write down the coordinates of A and D. (b) Find the coordinates of the centroid of ΔABC. (c) If D divides AC in the ratio k : 1, find the value of k. (d) Find the equation of the line BD.
questions.solution: (a) From the graph: A(0, 6) and D(−3, 0). (b) Centroid = ((x₁ + x₂ + x₃)/3, (y₁ + y₂ + y₃)/3) = ((0 + 4 − 4)/3, (6 − 4 − 2)/3) = (0, 0). [The printed solution mistakenly substitutes D(−3, 0) for C(−4, −2) and gets (1/3, 2/3); the correct centroid is (0, 0).] (c) D divides AC in ratio k : 1, A(0, 6) to C(−4, −2): x-coordinate: −3 = (−4k + 0)/(k + 1) ⇒ −3k − 3 = −4k ⇒ k = 3. (d) Line BD through B(4, −4) and D(−3, 0): slope = (−4 − 0)/(4 − (−3)) = −4/7. Equation: y − 0 = (−4/7)(x + 3) ⇒ 7y = −4x − 12 ⇒ 4x + 7y + 12 = 0.

marking_points.point: A(0, 6) and D(−3, 0) read from the graph
